title: Network Security
subtitle: Secure network devices, firewalls, VPNs and access from the edge to the endpoint
audience_line: Network administrators and engineers responsible for securing networks
overview: This programme teaches network engineers to secure the network itself. Participants harden device access and management, centralise authentication with AAA, filter traffic with ACLs, then deploy stateful, zone-based and next-generation firewalls, with a vendor-neutral lab on pfSense or OPNsense, and intrusion prevention. They secure endpoints and Layer 2, apply cryptography, build site-to-site and remote-access VPNs including WireGuard, compare them with zero trust network access, and test their defences. Every chapter ends with a lab, and the programme closes with a final project in which each team secures and validates a branch network.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Network administrators and engineers responsible for securing networks

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Switching and routing (course: Switching, Routing & Wireless Essentials (CCNA 2)), or equivalent. These are not taught again

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 51 h: 45 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs on simulated Cisco devices and open-source firewalls

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant (16 GB RAM) with Cisco Packet Tracer (free with each participant’s Cisco Networking Academy account) and pfSense or OPNsense and Linux VMs prepared by the trainer; isolated lab network; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project with validation tests; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can harden network devices, deploy AAA, ACLs, firewalls, IPS, Layer 2 protections and VPNs, and prove the result with security tests

phases.name: Securing Network Devices
phases.focus: Threats and mitigation, secure management, AAA, ACLs
phases.intro: Participants identify what needs protecting in a network, secure administrative access and management protocols, centralise authentication with RADIUS and TACACS+, and design and apply access control lists. Validated lab: routers managed only over SSH with AAA through a server, sending NTP-synchronised logs to a syslog server, and ACLs that enforce the security policy.

chapters.title: Device Access & Management
chapters.content: Secure access, administrative roles, SNMP, syslog, NTP

phases.name: Firewalls & IPS
phases.focus: Stateful and zone-based firewalls, NGFW, pfSense or OPNsense, Suricata, IPS
phases.intro: Participants build stateful and zone-based policy firewalls, learn what next-generation firewalls add, with application control, URL filtering, TLS inspection and Cisco Secure Firewall concepts, study IPS technologies and signatures, then deploy a vendor-neutral firewall on pfSense or OPNsense with NAT, VLANs and Suricata. Validated lab: a pfSense or OPNsense firewall that segments three VLANs and blocks a test attack with Suricata.

chapters.title: Next-Generation Firewalls
chapters.content: Application control, IPS, URL filtering, TLS inspection; Cisco Secure Firewall concepts

chapters.title: pfSense or OPNsense Lab
chapters.content: Rules, NAT, VLANs, IPS with Suricata

phases.name: Endpoint, Layer 2 & Cryptography
phases.focus: Endpoint protection, Layer 2 attacks and mitigation, integrity, authenticity, PKI
phases.intro: Participants protect endpoints and the switched network against Layer 2 attacks, then apply the cryptography that VPNs and management protocols rely on: hashing, signatures and certificates. Validated lab: a switch configured with port security, DHCP snooping and dynamic ARP inspection, verified with show commands, and a certificate issued by the lab certificate authority.

chapters.title: Endpoint & Layer 2 Security
chapters.content: Endpoint protection, Layer 2 attacks and mitigation

phases.name: VPNs, Zero Trust & Testing
phases.focus: Site-to-site IPsec, remote access with SSL and WireGuard, ZTNA, security testing
phases.intro: Participants connect sites with IPsec VPNs, give remote users access with IPsec, SSL VPN and WireGuard, compare these with zero trust network access, then test the network's defences with Nmap. Validated lab: two sites joined by an IPsec VPN, a remote user connected over WireGuard, and a scan report that confirms only the intended services are exposed.

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A secured branch network, validated by tests
phases.intro: Teams of two or three secure the network of a branch office from a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then prove their work with validation tests in front of the group.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, then deploy AAA, ACLs, a zone-based firewall or pfSense, IPS and Layer 2 security

chapters.title: VPN & Validation
chapters.content: Site-to-site IPsec VPN to head office; validation tests (show commands and simulation in Packet Tracer, Nmap against the pfSense or OPNsense segment)

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live tests in front of the group; questions and feedback

project.title: Securing a Branch Network
project.brief: A branch network secured end to end: AAA for device access, ACLs, a zone-based firewall or pfSense with IPS, Layer 2 protections and a site-to-site IPsec VPN to head office, each control proved by a validation test.
project.stack: Cisco Packet Tracer, Cisco IOS, RADIUS or TACACS+, pfSense or OPNsense, Suricata, IPsec, Nmap
project.deliverable: Configurations, network diagram, validation test plan and results, live demo
